papers.abs: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.

papers.abs: Atmospheric turbulence and channel loss represent the primary limiting factors in ground-to-satellite quantum communication systems, yet their joint impact remains insufficiently characterized across diverse operational conditions. In this work, we develop a comprehensive and open atmospheric channel model for quantum optical links along ground-to-satellite paths, integrating altitude-dependent molecular and aerosol absorptions. The model is validated with available data from missions such as Micius and Hispasat, including a secondary viability assessment for a hypothetical Starlink-based quantum communication network, where we evaluate the predicted channel behavior in terms of single-photon transmittance and power balance, alongside the channel capacity of the link for uplink and downlink exclusively. Our comparative analysis demonstrates the ability of our channel model to predict real data under simple atmospheric behavior assumptions, which offer practical guidelines for the design and optimization of future quantum satellite missions.

papers.abs: Coexistence of classical and quantum light in optical fiber is a key requirement for scalable quantum networks. However, it is fundamentally limited by nonlinear crosstalk from intense classical signals. Hollow-core fiber (HCF), with its intrinsically low optical nonlinearity, offers a promising solution. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the coexistence of polarization-entangled photons with dense wavelength-division multiplexed (DWDM) classical signals with a total launch power of 11.2 dBm, and perform a direct comparison between equal-length single-mode fiber (SMF) and photonic-bandgap-based HCF deployed in a campus network. We observe that HCF suppresses background noise by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to SMF, while preserving high-fidelity entanglement distribution. Our results provide clear experimental evidence of the advantage of HCF and establish its potential as a transmission medium.

papers.abs: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for exploring and manipulating topological optical states.

papers.abs: On-chip thermal processing is a key technology for materials discovery across all disciplines of the natural sciences. Here, we present a microfabricated heat-delivery platform that enables reaction-induced localized on-chip annealing up to 1400°C. A buried reactive multilayer combined with a nanometric diffusion barrier provide ultra-fast heating and quenching rates on the order of 10$^6$°C s$^{-1}$ as illustrated by the generation of ultra-high aspect ratio microstructures during rapid-solidification and the stabilization of dopant-free tetragonal zirconia at room temperature. Rapid kinetics also enable the observation of transient states of capillary-driven hole collapse in melts. Our work expands localized high-temperature processing routes and offers a material-independent approach for rapid screening of multidimensional nanomaterials on and off-equilibrium.

papers.abs: Radiation-pressure forces on transmissive optics, including dynamical backaction, are usually computed from the momentum flux of the external fields. For a dielectric of finite thickness, this omits the time dependence of the electromagnetic momentum stored inside. We compute the force on a lossless dielectric slab of arbitrary thickness $L_s$ submerged in a dielectric fluid, proceeding from both Lorentz force on its bound charges and from the external momentum fluxes for arbitrary carrier and sideband fields. We treat the surrounding medium through a prescribed linear dielectric response and do not model the accompanying mechanical response of the fluid, including pressure and electrostriction. These two methods both recover the expected force in the limit of a thin reflector, but differ in the more general case by the rate of change of the field momentum stored in the slab. papers.abs: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. papers.abs: The establishment of metrics and control of fundamental noise sources in quantum sensing is a long-standing goal in quantum science and technology. We report on the observation of polariton-mediated optical noise in a thermal Rydberg atom vapor and demonstrate its active control and suppression using a radio-frequency field in Rydberg electrometry. This reveals a nonlinear slow-light feedback mechanism in which the polariton medium stores and releases probe-field energy. We show that the reference radio-frequency field used in Rydberg heterodyne receivers can also tune the medium into an operating regime where high electromagnetic-field responsivity coincides with reduced optical noise. This operating-point control enables optimization of the electric-field sensitivity within the constraints imposed by Rydberg-polariton physics. papers.title: Spatiotemporal spherical Gaussian pulses
papers.abs: We describe a class of electromagnetic Gaussian modes with spherical spatiotemporal structure that remains invariant during propagation through anomalously dispersive media. The angular profile of the modes is given by spherical harmonics, whose quantization axis can be freely chosen. As a result, the modes support spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum (OAM) configurations with longitudinal and transverse components set by the orientation of the quantization axis. Superpositions of these modes generalize the familiar solution of a chirped pulse that simultaneously focuses and compresses to arbitrary angular structure. The modes are derived through a series of unitary transformations that map the dispersive paraxial wave equation onto a Schrödinger equation with a 3D isotropic harmonic potential. These transformations facilitate the identification of conserved operators for mixed longitudinal and transverse OAM.

papers.abs: Tapered optical fibers offer tunable dispersion and a small mode area, yielding high nonlinearity, which makes them ideal for nonlinear and quantum optics. Because phase-matched four-wave mixing strongly depends on dispersion, the taper diameter becomes a key parameter. For sub-micrometer tapers, identifying the exact diameter is challenging. Here, we show that when seeding with a broad spectrum, stimulated four-wave mixing yields a comb-like spectrum that is directly linked to the overall taper profile opening possibility for non-destructive evaluation of sub-micron taper. papers.title: Shaping the spectra of second harmonic laser by spatial focusing
papers.abs: Accurately controlling the spectral width of second harmonic generation (SHG) is critical in applications such as nonlinear microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and quantum optics, where tailored spectral properties are required. Although it is known that the focal length of the lens used to focus the pump beam influences the SHG spectrum, a simple and precise theoretical understanding of this effect has been lacking. Here, we develop a theoretical model to describe how pump focusing conditions affect SHG spectral broadening, and experimentally validate the model using BBO crystals with lenses of 50 mm and 200 mm focal lengths. Our results establish a practical method for engineering the SHG spectral width through pump focusing, providing valuable guidance for designing nonlinear optical systems with specific spectral requirements.

papers.abs: We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. papers.abs: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) remain localized despite the presence of extended modes at the same energy. In driven systems with long-range couplings, the absence of radiation does not by itself determine how a bound state decays in space. We study a Hermitian Rydberg spin waveguide coupled to a four-site plaquette, where a winding drive phase combines rotation with time translation to forbid propagating guide channels in one symmetry sector. The resulting eigenstate remains embedded in the continuum of other sectors and carries an inverse-cube waveguide amplitude, with coherent contributions from direct plaquette--guide coupling and long-range guide propagation. Pair-state calculations determine the microscopic couplings in the axial geometry, while coherent Floquet mixing sets the weight of the dominant circulating plaquette mode. The bound state thus retains the spatial signature of the long-range coupling even when radiation is forbidden.

papers.title: Symmetry-breaking chelation enables room-temperature all-optical spin coherence readout of aqueous Cu(II) for chemoselective discrimination
papers.abs: Optical initialization and readout of molecular electron spins in water remains challenging for 3d transition-metal complexes. Their Laporte-forbidden d-d transitions yield weak transition dipole moments, so optical spin detection in aqueous Cu(II) previously required ~1 M concentrations. Here we overcome this constraint through symmetry-breaking chelation. Coordinating Cu(II) with EDTA imposes a non-centrosymmetric ligand field with enhanced metal-ligand covalency, relaxing Laporte restrictions and amplifying d-d transition dipole moments. This design enhances absorption and magnetic circular dichroism by 7.3- and 5.6-fold, enabling ultrafast spin readout down to 100 μM with an apparent dephasing time T2^*~0.54 ns. As a proof-of-concept for selective molecular-spin sensing, histidine addition extends T_2^* to ~0.8 ns in a concentration-dependent manner, whereas glycine produces no measurable effect. These results show that symmetry breaking provides a strategy to create molecular spin-photon interfaces, opening avenues toward all-optical, analyte-responsive quantum sensing in water.

papers.abs: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) represents a fundamental degree of freedom (DoF) for understanding novel phenomena in solids and synthetic lattices. papers.abs: Quantum correlation measurements have emerged as a powerful tool for localizing multiple emitters with subwavelength separation. Multi-emitter localization consists of two distinct tasks: identifying the emitter count $N$ and estimating their positions $\left\{x^{i}\right\}$. We propose a method that directly infers the emitter count and positions from the multimodal data via learned inference. Symmetry and Quantum Interference in the Attosecond Domain
papers.abs: In this review, we examine the interplay of symmetry and quantum interference in the attosecond domain primarily through one- and two-electron photoelectron momentum distributions. Using our own work, we discuss how tailored laser fields provide control over dynamical symmetries, and how quantum-orbit methods make it possible to connect the resulting momentum-space structures to specific ionisation, propagation, and rescattering pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on ultrafast photoelectron holography and nonsequential double ionisation through recollision excitation with subsequent ionisation, where several distinct forms of quantum interference can be identified and manipulated. We also discuss how target properties, including the binding potential, orbital symmetry and parity, modify this mapping. Finally, we consider emerging opportunities offered by non-classical states of light, for which photon statistics and quantum fluctuations provide additional degrees of freedom for controlling symmetry and strong-field electron dynamics.

papers.title: Temperature dependence of a warm ensemble based memory on quantum communication rates
papers.abs: The success of long-distance quantum communication will hinge on quantum repeater nodes equipped with robust and scalable quantum memories. Such memories must possess specific operating characteristics to make these nodes practical. An attractive option for these memory devices is an atomic warm vapor system operating under the conditions of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT). These systems are easy to implement and require relatively low equipment overhead. A key metric in atomic-based quantum memory performance is optical depth, as it is closely tied to the strength of light-matter coupling. Here, we simulate and measure the optical depth-based performance of an EIT quantum memory using a warm atomic vapor cell. We then translate the simulated and measured optical depth and efficiency metrics into expected entanglement distribution rates. Our analysis evaluates the feasibility of these memories in optical quantum repeater nodes, which are essential for robust long-distance quantum communication.

This difference means that the standard Compton scattering formula cannot be applied to graphene simply by replacing c with vF. We first examine Compton-like scattering for a gapless Dirac carrier initially at the Dirac point and for a gapped carrier at the band edge, both corresponding to zero in-plane momentum. We then consider scattering from an energetic gapless Dirac carrier. By combining energy conservation with the graphene dispersion and in-plane momentum conservation, we obtain a quadratic equation for the scattered photon energy within the model considered. This relation is the main kinematic result of the work. papers.abs: Conservative nonlinear waves generally undergo an irreversible process of thermalization toward the Rayleigh--Jeans (RJ) equilibrium state. papers.title: Development of a fabrication-to-benchtop process for SiN-based quantum devices
papers.abs: Silicon nitride has emerged as a key material for the advancement of future quantum communication and computational devices. However, challenges persist in establishing a comprehensive development process, spanning from fabrication to optical characterization, essential for advancing these devices to their next stage of potential. Maintaining control over the entire process, from start to finish, alongside device modeling, enables more efficient and timely iteration and optimization. Here we introduce a fabrication-to-benchtop process. We employ an in-house stoichiometric recipe for device fabrication and conduct comprehensive characterization of optical losses and material properties. Understanding and controlling the refractive index of the device are vital for predicting device geometries and group indices. Implementing the refractive indices of our fabricated devices, we simulate microring resonators and demonstrate their application in generating optical solitons.

papers.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
papers.abs: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. papers.abs: Here, we demonstrate a novel optical self-injection-locking scheme integrated with a modulation-free laser frequency stabilization technique co-integrated with a compact vacuum-gap micro-Fabry-Perot cavity (uFP), with Q-factor of 3.46E9, to realize an ultra-stable laser with sub-Hz fundamental linewidth using a silicon photonic chip. The chip is fabricated using the Advanced Micro Foundry standard silicon photonic process and occupies a footprint of 10 mm^2.

papers.abs: Experiments realizing strong interactions in partially filled Chern bands have observed fractional Chern insulators (FCIs), superconductors, and topological crystals in close proximity. We characterize the competing phases and identify key features of the experimental phenomenology. FCIs from the Jain sequence transition into chiral p-wave superconductivity both below and above half filling as the band dispersion is enhanced. By contrast, at half filling, a generalized Hall crystal with quantized Hall conductance and a doubled unit cell forms for sufficiently strong coupling. papers.title: Classical Capacity of Single-Mode Bosonic Gaussian Channels
papers.abs: The classical capacity of a noisy optical channel is the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted reliably, given a constraint on the mean input energy. For the ubiquitous bosonic Gaussian channels, which include standard models of loss and noise in fibre and free-space optical links, determining this rate requires addressing whether entanglement between channel uses or non-Gaussian signals can outperform Gaussian encodings. More precisely, the question is whether the energy-constrained Holevo information is additive across arbitrarily many channel uses and coincides with its Gaussian counterpart. We answer these fundamental questions in the affirmative for every single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel at every input energy. Namely, we prove that independently prepared Gaussian states with Gaussian-distributed random displacements achieve the capacity, including in the low-energy regime where squeezing the signals competes with encoding information in their displacement. Programmable all-to-all entangling gates for cavity-coupled atoms
papers.abs: Fault tolerant quantum computers greatly benefit from having both high fidelity entangling gates and a non-local qubit connectivity. However, most entangling gates for neutral atoms are local, requiring separated atoms to be moved using optical tweezers to yield entanglement between them. Here, we design a high fidelity Mølmer Sørensen-like entangling gate between neutral atoms coupled to a photonic cavity, enabling a programmable all-to-all connectivity through the shared cavity coupling. The gate is both robust to changes in cavity photon number, and enables selective entanglement between any subset of separated atoms through local laser addressing. This eliminates the need to physically move atoms to perform the gate, and therefore motional errors and erasure are suppressed. Using experimentally realistic parameters we demonstrate gate fidelities exceeding $F > 0.99$, with higher fidelities achievable through optimal control of the pump amplitudes.

papers.abs: Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are multipartite entangled quantum states that play a central role in quantum information theory, with applications in quantum communication, cryptography, and distributed quantum computing. A major experimental goal is to create high-dimensional GHZ states using multiple entangled parties. Krenn, Gu and Zeilinger discovered a surprising bridge between these quantum-optical experiments and graph theory: certain photonic experiments can be represented by edge-coloured, edge-weighted graphs, and the dimension of the produced GHZ state equals the number of feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colourings. This led Krenn and Gu to conjecture that every GHZ graph with more than four vertices has dimension at most $2$. A counterexample would give a new high-dimensional multipartite GHZ construction, while a proof would clarify fundamental resource limitations in quantum optics. papers.abs: Recent work has demonstrated that it is possible to generate frequency combs in normal dispersion microresonators by taking advantage of fabricated mode coupling that induces a mode split. In contrast to frequency combs generated by microresonators in the anomalous dispersion regime, which are typically generated using bright solitons, the frequency combs generated by normal dispersion regime microresonators are dark pulses that are commonly referred to as dark solitons or platicons. Our work reveals a broad region of stability for platicons. papers.abs: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. papers.abs: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference underpins many photonic quantum information protocols and is commonly characterized by a single visibility parameter. This quantity is typically obtained by averaging over a fixed coincidence window, thereby discarding details of the underlying temporal structure that are critical in continuous-wave processes. Four-photon interference with continuous-wave sources furthermore requires photon pairs with long coherence times, which we generate in microring resonators and measure with ultrafast time-resolved detection. Here, we model and resolve their interference and temporal structure by recording all four photon arrival times and mapping their relative delays onto a three-dimensional coincidence histogram relative to a trigger detection. The resulting structure preserves relative arrival-time correlations that are usually discarded and enables post-processed optimization of coincidence windows to trade off visibility against count rate. This method provides a general benchmark for continuous-wave sources in interference-based quantum network protocols.

papers.abs: Multi-aperture reception converts spatial diversity into a coherent-combining gain, but only if the relative phase and polarization of the collected field replicas are aligned before they are summed. In a satellite-to-ground downlink the atmosphere perturbs amplitude, phase and polarization, so the alignment must track a fluctuating channel rather than a fixed offset. papers.title: Microwave spectroscopic evidence of a moiré-commensurate electron crystal in monolayer graphene
papers.abs: We probe the conductivity of the lowest Landau level of a moiré-aligned monolayer graphene device by broadband microwave transmission through a coplanar waveguide ($\sim$50 mK, 15.4--18 T), isolating the longitudinal channel through a low-minus-high frequency band difference $D(ν)$. We resolve a series of minima in $D(ν)$ that drift with field along lines of fixed carrier density rather than fixed Landau filling, the hallmark of moiré-commensurate electron crystals. The strongest minimum is present at every field and matches no fractional quantum Hall or integer Hofstadter state. It lies at band filling $s=1/3$, one electron for every three moiré cells---the generalized Wigner crystal that DaSilva, Jung, and MacDonald predict as the most favorable fixed-density ($t=0$) commensuration. The weaker minima fall near neighboring commensurate fillings.

papers.abs: Distributing entanglement directly between error-corrected logical qubits is an important capability for scalable quantum networks. The protocol combines motional-control and photonic-networking operations that have already been demonstrated in trapped-ion experiments.

papers.abs: Quantum measurements not only extract information but also reshape quantum evolution through measurement backaction. Here, we investigate periodic conditional measurements, in which coherent evolution is repeatedly interrupted by local measurements. We show that the bright and dark modes of the conditional evolution operator provide a unified spectral description of both the post-selected final state along no-detection trajectories and the statistics of detection events. Using a three-dimensional photonic chip, we demonstrate on-demand state engineering through dark-mode preservation and bright-mode selection, enabling the protection of topological corner states and excited-state shelving. We further observe the predicted transition of the total detection probability on an effectively infinite one-dimensional lattice and identify its microscopic origin in Floquet near-dark modes. These results establish periodic conditional measurements as a general framework for engineering conditional quantum states and manipulating event-detection statistics in monitored quantum dynamics.

papers.abs: Integrating Rydberg-state control of atom-atom interactions with cavity control of atom-light interactions enables the combination of local entangling operations with photon-mediated long-range coupling, measurement, and communication. papers.abs: We demonstrate control between level repulsion and level attraction of photon-magnon coupling spectra in a chiral microwave-photon resonator loaded with a 2 mm YIG sphere. By systematically varying the coupling mode volume via the YIG position and the dc-field orientation, we tune the ratio between coherent and dissipative coupling strengths, $J/Γ$, and thereby switch between level repulsion and level attraction in the hybrid spectra. Full-wave electromagnetic and magnetization-dynamics simulations reveal multiple photon-magnon hybrid modes with distinct spatial overlap factors, which quantitatively account for gap sizes and their angular dependence. Strong nonreciprocity appears near $J/Γ\approx 1$, yielding 28.6 dB isolation ratio in agreement with a unified single-bath input-output model and full-wave simulations. Angular dependence of spectral characterization confirms a picture of the chirality-selection rule and our method of geometric tuning might be useful for considering reconfigurable on-chip isolators.

In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. papers.abs: Embedding materials in optical cavities has emerged as a powerful strategy for controlling their physical properties. In this context, increasing attention has been devoted to the thermal Purcell effect, which describes how the radiative heat transfer between a material and its photonic environ- ment can be modified by the electromagnetic boundary conditions imposed by the cavity. Here, we investigate near-field effects in cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer in planar cavities composed of realistic, dissipative gold mirrors, extending previous work that considered ideal mirrors. We iden- tify the conditions under which near-field effects lead to a substantial enhancement of heat transfer between the material and a photonic thermal bath relative to free space, owing to the strong modi- fication of the photonic local density of states by evanescent modes within the cavity. In particular, we find that radiative heat flow can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude in cavities ranging from nanometer to micrometer scales, depending on the absorber frequency and dipole orientation.

papers.abs: Spatial sectioning of the far-field noncollinear field from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is a promising approach for multiparty quantum communication. Although demonstrations with six pairs of users have been reported, the fundamental limits remain unknown. These include the maximum number of channels, the required degree of channel optimization, and the dependence on input parameters. In this paper, we provide a practical framework that answers these questions by connecting input parameters and invoking a design theorem. For a representative configuration, we realize 12 user-pair channels with routing consistency exceeding $0.9999$ at a $12\%$ reduction in photon flux. We further show that sectioning improves the accidental-coincidence budget linearly with the number of channels $N$, allowing the aggregate key rate to scale with the user count. These results provide a design strategy for spatial-division multiplexing of entangled photons analogous to the channel-spacing standards used in wavelength-division networks.

papers.abs: This paper reconstructs the Michelson interference phenomenon based solely on the binary (on-off) statistics of a single-photon counter and macroscopic path-difference data, without the a priori assumptions of complex wave superposition or prior spectral information. In contrast to the conventional approach that assumes light as a continuous complex wave function and considers interference between them, this study focuses on the algebraic properties inherent in discrete detection statistics. papers.abs: The search for new degrees of freedom (DoF) of light is central to advancing optical information encoding and multiplexing. papers.abs: The optical Kerr effect in high-refractive-index membrane metasurfaces patterned with a square lattice of five-pointed star-shaped pores is investigated numerically using gallium phosphide as a model material. The star geometry supports resonances with pronounced electromagnetic energy confinement, including an anapole state. The sharp tips of the star-shaped pores concentrate the electric energy density in air, exceeding that of Mie voids by a factor of seven. The effective second-order refractive index is enhanced by up to three orders of magnitude relative to bulk GaP, with the largest values obtained near the anapole resonances. The nonlinear response remains stable under polarization rotation and random misalignment of the nanoholes, indicating tolerance to fabrication imperfections. These results establish star-shaped pore lattices in freestanding membranes as a promising platform for nonlinear optics exploiting strong field confinement.

papers.abs: Phononic integrated circuits enable the development of compact systems to manipulate radio frequency signals through interconnected networks of acoustic waveguides. Electron-Mediated Phonon Polaritons in Quantum Cavities
papers.abs: Phonon-photon coupling in quantum materials is commonly treated as an effective direct interaction, neglecting the crucial role played by electrons. Here we develop a gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons that captures electronic screening, dissipation, and hybridization. We show that screening can suppress polariton formation in metals, severely constraining cavity control of phonon-mediated superconductivity. By contrast, interband electronic resonances in time-reversal-symmetric gapped systems can strongly enhance phonon-photon coupling, enabling robust polariton formation down to the monolayer limit despite electronic absorption. We illustrate these effects in NbSe2, hBN, and gapped graphene. Finally, we show that gauge invariance enforces photon decoupling from a critical soft phonon, establishing a general no-go mechanism for photon condensation.

papers.abs: We study quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and secret-key generation through multimode bosonic loss and fading channels, assisted by local quantum operations and two-way classical communication. Using sector teleportation, we determine the exact two-way quantum and secret-key capacities of multimode pure-loss channels under a mean photon-number constraint, allowing arbitrary adaptive quantum protocols. We extend these results to continuous frequency-dependent loss under a power constraint and identify the optimal allocation of photons among optical modes. For constant loss over an unlimited bandwidth, we obtain a closed-form capacity proportional to the square root of power. For randomly varying loss, we determine exact finite-energy capacities when the channel realization is publicly revealed, distinguishing knowledge before and after transmission. papers.abs: The valence-bond-glass state of the 4d^1 double perovskite Ba2YMoO6 combines Mo^5+ singlets with residual paramagnetic "orphan" spins whose coupling is hard to reach with bulk probes. We probe them by electron paramagnetic resonance of a dilute Gd^3+ ion on the Y^3+ site via broadband coplanar-waveguide transmission at 5 K. The isostructural nonmagnetic niobate Ba2YNbO6, doped with the same Gd^3+ probe, is a fixed-lattice control. The Gd^3+ linewidth nearly doubles in the magnetic host. Dipolar coupling to the sparse orphans is nearly an order of magnitude too weak; the excess is instead reproduced by a transferred f-d superexchange of J ~ 0.2 K, so the width is a static measure of orphan-spin coupling. The half-field (Delta m_S = +/-2) satellite collapses in the magnetic host, a dynamical dephasing channel, while the unchanged g-factor marks a zero-mean random internal field. Together the two channels probe the coupling and dynamics of valence-bond-glass orphan spins.

papers.abs: We study collective charge excitations in pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals within the random-phase approximation, considering both the linearised model with a flat-band and its quadratic-corrected counterpart. We analyse their density response, Drude weights, screening, plasmon dispersion and damping, particle-hole continua, and Friedel oscillations from the long-wavelength to the arbitrary-momentum regime. The quadratic correction renders the flat-band dispersive and endows it with a Fermi surface, thereby affecting the overall response. Comparisons with Weyl and Hopf semimetals reveal how bandstructure and quantum geometry jointly govern collective charge dynamics. While the Drude weights are determined by the Fermi surface and band-velocities, interband screening, plasmon dispersion, and Friedel oscillations reflect the quantum geometry of the eigenstates.

papers.abs: Mode locking is the mechanism by which lasers organize many optical modes into stable trains of ultrashort pulses. papers.abs: Kagome lattices provide a simple geometry for engineering electronic states that exhibit novel quantum behavior. In conventional kagome materials, however, the relevant states are often embedded in chemically complex three-dimensional crystals and are difficult to isolate or tune. Molecule-based kagome networks offer structural precision and tunability, but have largely been confined to metallic substrates incompatible with 2D devices. Here we report growth of single-layer Ni$_3$(HITP)$_2$ metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) on van der Waals substrates including graphene-based field-effect devices using metal-salt molecular beam epitaxy. Low-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy resolves kagome-derived flat-band and van Hove singularity-based spectral features consistent with first-principles calculations. Gating hybrid 2D MOF devices allows us to energetically shift kagome spectral features, thus establishing electrostatic control of chemically programmable 2D kagome electronic lattices.

papers.abs: We report continuous-wave (CW) vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) generation at 148.4 nm by second-harmonic generation of 296.8-nm fundamental light in quasi-phase matched (QPM) BaMgF4 (BMF). At the incident power of 170 mW, a VUV output power of approximately 31 pW can be obtained. The quadratic dependence of the signal on the incident power in the QPM region and its attenuation in the ambient environment support the identification of VUV generation. The polarization dependence shows a sine-function shape with a 15% output attenuation from the maximum to the minimum. These results highlight the potential of BMF as a nonlinear medium for CW VUV generation.

papers.abs: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. papers.title: A complete quantum process model for physically realistic photo-detection in the joint photon-number and spectral degrees of freedom
papers.abs: Photo-detection is a fundamental component of experimental photonics, yet theoretical models often treat detectors solely in the photon-number basis, neglecting other relevant degrees of freedom such as spectral characteristics. We present a complete quantum process model for physically realistic photodetection that incorporates both photon-number effects and frequency-dependent detector response, described through explicitly derived Kraus operators in the operator-sum representation. This formalism accommodates realistic inefficiencies, models detection within finite spectral windows, and can be directly substituted for idealized models in quantum optical analyses. The model leads to identifying the suitable detection window of the detectors relative to the spectral distribution of incident photons and conversely, in order to maximize the observability of quantum effects.

papers.abs: Chip-scale microresonator-based frequency combs, commonly referred to as microcombs, are promising sources for field-deployable metrology applications. papers.title: Scalable long-distance quantum fan-out gates with reduced resource overhead
papers.abs: Scalable long-distance quantum gates are essential for distributed quantum computation and scalable quantum networks. We propose an efficient scheme for implementing an $n$-qubit fan-out gate $C^n$ (also known as a controlled-NOT-$\cdots$-NOT gate) across spatially separated parties. Our protocol requires only a pre-shared $n$-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state, $n$ local controlled-NOT (CNOT) gates, and feed-forward operations, thereby reducing both the CNOT and Hadamard gate counts by $(n-2)$ when compared with the standard decomposition-based approach. We further develop two optical architectures to implement the heralded and post-selected $n$-photon fan-out gates, respectively. These schemes require fewer single photons resources and achieve higher success probabilities than their decomposition-based counterparts, representing significant improvements. The results indicate that our approach is experimentally feasible and pave the way toward practical long-distance quantum computation.

papers.abs: We investigate the collective emission spectra and photon correlations of two identical dipole-dipole-coupled emitters under continuous-wave (CW) and periodic pulsed driving. Our results show that a periodic train of instantaneous $π_x$ pulses can generate emission spectra whose dominant features closely resemble those obtained under CW excitation. We find that the structure of the collective emission spectra reflects the interplay among the resonance conditions, dipole-dipole coupling, and the inter-pulse delay $τ_D$. We further demonstrate that finite-duration $π_x$ pulses with sufficiently high Rabi frequencies can closely reproduce the ideal instantaneous-pulse limit. In contrast to the emission spectra, the photon correlations $g^{(2)}(t,τ)$ are governed primarily by $τ_D$ and, unlike under CW driving, become increasingly insensitive to the resonance conditions in the short-pulse limit. These results establish periodic pulsed driving as a versatile means of tailoring both the emission spectra and the photon statistics of coupled two-emitter systems.

papers.abs: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in physics research is increasingly common, yet few guidelines exist for its effective use. Starting with a principles-based approach, we outline a set of ten requirements for collaborative AI agents in experimental physics, spanning scientific norms, effective agent use, and domain expertise. We take a human-centered approach in which agents act as collaborators that amplify rather than replace the expertise of a human researcher (user) who directs the work and is responsible for its results. We then present a framework designed to enforce these requirements, detailing methods for improving off-the-shelf behavior of large language models (LLMs) with custom scaffolding and describing general-purpose scientific workflows and skills. papers.abs: Structured light provides a powerful means of controlling matter while itself exhibiting nontrivial spatial topology. Here, we show that these spatial structures can be harnessed to locally engineer the topological properties of matter. In a paradigmatic example of a topological insulator with Dirac surface states driven by an optical skyrmion beam, we show that structured light spatially tailors the effective Hamiltonian, yielding position-dependent topological gaps and Dirac velocities. The resulting gap modulation can create topological and trivial regions separated by optically defined interfaces, without introducing material boundaries or chemical modifications. We further show that the geometry of these interfaces can be controlled through the spatial structure of the light, in particular its orbital angular momentum. Our results establish structured light as a route to dynamically pattern topological phases and open a broader perspective on the interplay between topology in light and matter, including the possibility of transferring topological characteristics between the two.

papers.abs: We have developed an apparatus for the measurement of the acousto-electric effect (AEE) from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperatures. The AEE is excited by bulk acoustic waves (BAWs) for which a lithium niobate piezoelectric actuator is employed. A very low background noise level is realized through careful electrical and mechanical design of the setup. The validity of the setup is tested by measuring the AEE in heavily doped P-type and N-type silicon. The opposite sign of the AEE signal was seen for both samples, showing dependence of the signal on the type of charge carrier being dragged by acoustic waves. The signal showed quadratic dependence on the driving voltage, which is consistent with the AEE literature. Further, a temperature dependence of the AEE signal was measured, which exhibits a monotonic increase with a rise in temperature. The ability to probe the AEE in bulk samples at low temperatures makes this setup a promising tool to investigate the AEE and related phenomena in different materials at cryogenic temperatures.

papers.abs: Quantum teleportation, a key building block for quantum technologies, enables distant parties, Alice and Bob, to transfer an unknown quantum state using entanglement, local operations, and classical communication. In this work, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for single-photon time-frequency continuous variables, where time is the time of arrival at a detector. We detail the operational requirements of the protocol, notably the nonlinear interactions needed for the photon-photon time-frequency entangling gate. This results in a trade-off between teleportation fidelity and the temporal bandwidth of the input photon wavepacket. The protocol itself can be used for remote detector synchronization. Adaptive Entanglement Witnessing for Two-Qubit Systems
papers.abs: Entanglement witnesses are a key instrument in determining the entanglement of unknown bipartite qubit systems without requiring a full tomography. Riccardi et al. (2020) proposed a set of two-qubit witnesses, denoted $\{W^3\}$, which require a set of local measurements in three bases. In this work we propose an additional set of witnesses, denoted $\{W^5\}$, that build on $\{W^3\}$ and require measurements in two additional bases. We present an adaptive two-step method that uses the measurement results obtained for $\{W^3\}$ to select which $W^5$ to evaluate. We computationally demonstrate that our adaptive two-step protocol can identify 72% of entangled states generated according to the methods of Roik et al. (2021) while requiring measurements in only five of the nine bases needed for full quantum tomography. Additionally, we experimentally verify the behavior of both sets of witnesses using polarization-entangled photon pairs.

papers.abs: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers and could avoid potential laboratory-based uncertainties. Therefore, in this study, artificial intelligence is implemented to estimate the optical constants of two types of materials, i.e., noble metals, and semiconductors. To this end, an artificial neural network is used to estimate the real and the imaginary parts of the refractive index of a specific material for various wavelengths of light. papers.title: Photon-efficient readout of optical cavity arrays via spatial heterodyne
papers.abs: Optical cavity arrays are an emerging tool for efficiently interfacing optical photons to quantum emitters for applications such as quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate a metrology technique for such cavity arrays by interfering cavity array outputs against a tilted reference beam on a camera, constituting a spatial heterodyne. Both the amplitude and phase of each cavity's transmitted field can be extracted from the resulting images. Enabled by the improved scaling of heterodyne detection over intensity detection in the presence of technical noise, we demonstrate signal-to-noise ratio greater than one down to the single detected photon level, even in the presence of hundreds of noise equivalent photons. This readout technique holds promise for fast, non-destructive imaging of atomic qubits in cavity arrays by requiring fewer scattered photons while allowing the use of fast cameras with higher electronic readout noise.

papers.abs: Context: Low polarization in an unresolved source may reflect weak local polarization or spatial cancellation between strongly polarized regions. Aims: We develop a general theoretical framework for occultation polarimetry and determine what information can be inferred directly from unresolved full Stokes light curves, without reconstructing a polarization image or prescribing a source model. Methods: For a stationary, spatially incoherent source undergoing monotonic occultation, we relate Stokes variations to the polarization sampled by an arbitrarily curved occulting boundary and derive an exact variance decomposition of the normalized Stokes vector. papers.abs: Low-loss stoichiometric silicon nitride on oxidized silicon has emerged as the major wide-band photonics platform for nonlinear and quantum photonics. These films, deposited by low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD), are well known to have around 1000 MPa of residual tensile stress, which often leads to cracking when film thickness exceeds 400 nm. Although various stress-mitigation approaches can isolate or prevent cracking, this stress issue remains a major fabrication challenge. Low-residual-stress LPCVD stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire has also been reported and recently explored for photonics at telecommunication wavelengths. Here, we advance its development through systematic characterization, including thin-film stress analysis, ellipsometry and prism-coupling measurements of refractive index and loss, and swept-wavelength spectroscopy of fabricated photonic devices across a broad range of wavelengths. papers.abs: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. papers.abs: Unidirectional transport of light is a central capability in photonics, enabling critical functionalities such as isolation and routing. Ordinarily, this directionality depends on the mode of light, but not its phase. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate phase-dependent unidirectional transport of light for the first time. Specifically, we realize a system where conjugate quadratures of an optical field decouple and propagate in opposite directions. Our all-optical approach uses multiple pump frequencies in a high-$Q$ nanophotonic micro-resonator to achieve Hamiltonian programming through Kerr nonlinearity. Even though we rely on optical nonlinearity, our approach is not limited to any minimal power requirement on the signal. We demonstrate the ultimate limit of this by measuring the effect of quadrature-dependent transport on vacuum fluctuations. Our approach unlocks a fundamental new capability for controlling light, and can enable previously inaccessible regimes of phase-sensitive directional amplification, sensing, and routing.

papers.abs: Intense ultrafast lasers are the backbone of strong-field physics and enable table-top scale applications of coherent high-photon energy radiation through high-harmonic generation (HHG). Using short-wavelength drivers in HHG promises highly efficient conversion into the extreme ultraviolet, but short pulse durations are essential to this approach. We generate multi-GW peak power, sub-10 fs pulses in the visible with broad spectral tunability (220--752 nm) by harnessing soliton dynamics in large-core, gas-filled capillary fibers for high-energy resonant dispersive wave emission. This establishes the potential of resonant dispersive waves as a new class of driving lasers for HHG and strong-field physics in addition to widespread applications in ultrafast spectroscopy.

papers.abs: Weak measurement has proven useful for metrology, for probing quantum paradoxes, and for the direct measurement of quantum states. Weak measurements of polarization qubits with temporal pointers provide a direct route to weak-value characterization, including in regimes where the pointer is only partially coherent. We derive a closed-form expression for the post-selected temporal shift that interpolates between the incoherent and coherent (ideal) weak-measurement limits through a single parameter $ν$, the pointer visibility. The expression is experimentally tested for a range of polarization states spanning three trajectories corresponding to rotations about the principal axes of the Poincaré sphere. Two of the trajectories provide parameter-free benchmarks, with the real part of the weak value following $\cos^2θ$ and $1/2$. In contrast, the weak value along the third trajectory is sensitive to incoherence and is well described by the single-parameter partial-coherence model, from which a reduced pointer visibility is obtained. papers.title: Ultra-low-loss Ta2O5 waveguide for integrated nonlinear photonics
papers.abs: Integrated nonlinear photonics demands waveguides that simultaneously offer ultra-low-loss, relatively strong nonlinearity, and tight mode confinement. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) is attractive for this purpose because it combines a broad transparency window, relatively strong third-order nonlinearity, and favorable thick-film growth characteristics. In tightly confined Ta2O5 waveguides, however, enhanced interaction between the optical mode and etched sidewalls makes scattering loss an important limitation for achieving high Q anomalous-dispersion resonators. Here, we mitigate this confinement-scattering trade-off in pure Ta2O5 waveguides using a fabrication flow based on the Damascene concept. The resulting microring resonators (MRRs) with a cross-section of 1.6 μm x 0.85 μm exhibit intrinsic quality factors exceeding 4.0 x 106, corresponding to propagation losses below 10 dB/m, while maintaining anomalous dispersion suitable for bright dissipative Kerr soliton operation. papers.abs: Superradiance is a collective optical effect where emitters cooperatively radiate with a maximal intensity scaling proportional to the square of the number of emitters. Despite the superradiant cascade transitioning through highly entangled states, it has been shown that, for dynamics along the Dicke ladder, superradiance need not generate entanglement between the emitters. By contrast, we show how introducing incoherent local processes -- normally considered detrimental to both entanglement and superradiance -- can generate high levels of inter-emitter entanglement. We develop a general framework, using degenerate non-Hermitian perturbation theory, for the study of superradiant Liouvillian steady-state degeneracy breaking by these local operations from a few emitters up into the thermodynamic limit. From this, we are able to show that entanglement becomes ubiquitous in this regime and demonstrate its robustness against other forms of symmetric environmental noise. Meanwhile, four-wave mixing acts to stabilize intermodal phase relationships, facilitating selective STML characterized by diverse mode compositions with matched group velocities. Spatiotemporal solitons containing the pure LP01 mode, degenerate LP11 modes, or LP02+LP21 composite modes are selectively realized and mapped across the parameter space spanned by intracavity gain and filter detuning. papers.abs: Bismuth oxyselenide (Bi2O2Se) has emerged as a leading semiconductor candidate for next-generation electronics and quantum phenomena research. However, its strong ionic interlayer bonding of Se layers fundamentally restricts the full potential of this otherwise promising quasi-two-dimensional (2D) material. In this work, we demonstrate chlorine substitution as an effective strategy to introduce van der Waals gaps and modify the electronic structure of the system. Through comprehensive transport and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on Bi6O6Se2Cl2 single crystal, an optimal Cl-doping compound, we show that the key electronic features, including indirect band gap, high electron mobility, and carrier effective mass, are well preserved, while the 2D character of the system is sufficiently enhanced. papers.title: Maximal Axion Optical Chirality Enabled by Degenerate Quasibound States in the Continuum
papers.abs: Axion quasiparticles introduce magnetoelectric coupling in topological materials, yet their optical signatures are intrinsically weak, severely limiting experimental detection and practical exploitation. Here, we demonstrate maximal optical chirality of axion quasiparticles by coupling them with degenerate quasibound states in the continuum (qBICs). By integrating three-dimensional topological insulators (3DTIs) with achiral photonic crystal slabs (PCSs), we reveal that axion quasiparticles induce an effective Zeeman effect that lifts the degeneracy of achiral qBICs in PCSs, splitting them into two nondegenerate high-Q chiral qBICs with maximally opposite chirality. These result in a more than 10^3- and 200-fold increase in the polarization conversion efficiency and Faraday rotation angle, respectively, compared to the intrinsic chiroptical response of bare 3DTI films. Moreover, circular dichroism and nonreciprocal optical responses are revealed as new key signatures for probing axion quasiparticles in 3DTI-PCS coupled systems. papers.abs: Synthetic three-dimensional (3D) light fields provide a new route to imprinting chirality on achiral matter through light--matter interaction. Although previous work has numerically demonstrated that chirality can be imprinted on the photoelectron momentum spectrum of atoms, a transparent analytical physical picture that links the structure of the driving field to the chirality of the spectrum is still an open question. Here, using frequency-domain theory based on nonperturbative quantum electrodynamics (QED), we demonstrate that this chirality originates from coherence between adjacent quantum transition channels. papers.abs: Sensing time-varying signals is essential for precision measurement and for characterizing fluctuations in physical systems. In this work, we show that quantum entanglement provides an exponential advantage in the acquisition time required to learn the temporal statistics of a stationary classical signal. The task is to estimate the characteristic function of joint displacements on selected bosonic modes within a fixed-duration window, using continuous measurements of one signal realization. We present an entanglement-assisted scheme based on two-mode squeezed probes and local Bell measurements with protected idlers, and bound its acquisition time accounting for readout noise and correlations between signal windows. For a strictly stationary pulse family, it achieves polynomial acquisition time at inverse-polynomial accuracy with logarithmic squeezing and polynomial photon number. papers.title: Fast local field calculation in cascaded coupled systems
papers.abs: Computing the field within a sub-unit of cascaded systems is a recurring problem in wave physics. It is central to gradient-based inverse design, in situations where only a region of the system is modified while the rest remains fixed. Standard approaches either resimulate the entire cascade at every change, or require a detailed characterization of every surrounding sub-system. Both become impractical when many design iterations are needed. Here, we introduce a hybrid method combining the $S$-matrix approach, which propagates fields through cascaded systems, with the Green's function method, which gives the field generated by a source within a characterized system. In this approach, the sub-systems surrounding the region of interest need only be characterized once, after which the local field can be recomputed rapidly for any new configuration. We validate the method on a disordered lossy waveguide, finding excellent agreement with finite-element simulations. papers.title: Definition of Multi-Parameter Super-Resolution for Optical Telescopes
papers.abs: Super-resolution techniques in microscopy are opening new frontiers in biology, and super-resolution for telescope imaging may provide similar benefits for astronomy and space domain awareness. Telescope super-resolution techniques such as multi-plane light conversion and photonic lanterns have been inspired by the ability of mode sorting measurements to extract classical Fisher information closer to the quantum bound than standard telescope imaging. Furthermore, there has been no demonstration of an estimation algorithm with performance that follows the limit set by the Fisher information when all point source parameters are considered. papers.abs: Understanding how pairing correlations in superconductors evolve out of equilibrium is a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. In systems with $s$-wave pairing, the character of Cooper pairing evolves continuously from a BCS regime of weakly bound, overlapping pairs to a BEC regime of tightly bound molecules, each with distinct excitation spectra. Here we realize and probe pairing dynamics across these regimes using cold, non-degenerate $^{87}$Rb atoms coupled to an optical cavity with Floquet dressing. Our cavity-QED platform emulates fermionic superfluids through a mapping onto Anderson pseudospins, while optical and microwave control tunes the ratio of interactions to single-particle energies, providing a flexible approach complementary to ultracold Feshbach and ultrafast solid-state platforms. Selecting diffraction-order pairs produces correlation kernels containing either the product or the conjugate product of two input field envelopes. Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abs: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials. These findings open a new avenue for designing nonlinear chiroptical materials which harness the duality of polarity and chirality and chemical versatility of COFs.

We propose three real-valued, positive landscapes built from the Feinberg--Zee hermitization of G: a regularised Gramian inverse (Gram), the diagonal Schur block that carries the Metz--Neri--Rogers spectral density (SY), and the full hermitized inverse contracted against a polarization-isotropic source pair (Herm). The three form a progression from spectrum-blind to fully hermitisation-faithful, agree in the limit $z\to 0$, and diverge where it matters: at nonzero spectral shift SY resolves modes that Gram collapses, and Herm resolves modes that SY collapses. papers.abs: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. papers.abs: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. papers.abs: We investigate the construction of unitary $t$-designs in a multi-photon Fock space on programmable linear-optical interferometers. Using the frame potential as the optimization objective, we identify architectures that realize approximate unitary 1- and 2-designs with considerably fewer controllable parameters than required for universal linear optics. For example, we find numerical evidence suggesting that for unitary 1-designs, the required number of programmable parameters scales empirically as $2d$ with the number of modes $d$, instead of $O(d^2)$. We benchmark the resulting ensembles using single-photon transition probabilities and average channel fidelities. Furthermore, as a practical result, we develop a photon-number estimation protocol for multi-photon Fock states that leverages these optimized 1- and 2-designs. Our findings demonstrate that shallow interferometers can accurately reproduce Haar-averaged first moments, while second-moment-sensitive observables provide a considerably stricter test for approximate unitary 2-designs.

papers.abs: Broadband soliton microcombs near 1 $μ$m offer coherent, evenly spaced optical lines for measurements in the biological window. However, combining broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines increases the pump-power requirement and makes thermally stable soliton access more difficult. Here, we demonstrate broadband silicon nitride (Si3N4) soliton microcombs enabled by a resonant coupler that enhances pump delivery to the nonlinear resonator. The device generates a spectrum spanning 930-1380 nm with an approximately 98-GHz comb-line spacing at on-chip pump powers of tens of milliwatts, while providing reliable thermally stable access to the single-soliton state. These results provide a route to compact, power-efficient microcomb sources that combine broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines for spectroscopy and imaging in the biological window.

Temporal chirality in Floquet photonic media
papers.abs: We reveal temporal chirality in time-modulated photonic media: reversing the orientation of a closed loop traced by the complex permittivity can leave the Floquet spectrum unchanged while strongly modifying the directional scattering response under the same excitation. This behavior is linked to two symmetry constraints on the evolution operator, namely pseudo-Hermiticity and pseudo-unitarity. We prove the general occurrence of temporal chirality based on a complex Bogoliubov parametrization of the scattering amplitudes. We illustrate these findings in a single-harmonic temporal-$\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric system: both modulation-loop orientations support the same vacuum-like Floquet photonic bands at the phase transition, but one suppresses backward photon generation whereas the other induces strong growth, as confirmed by full-wave simulations. Our results establish temporal chirality as a distinct notion in time-varying photonics and identify modulation-loop orientation as a control knob for Floquet wave dynamics.

A Gauge-Invariant Clustering Coefficient for Complex-Weighted Bipartite Networks
papers.abs: Structural measures such as the clustering coefficient and the average shortest-path length characterise how a network is organised. These measures are typically formulated for real, non-negative edge weights. A class of quantum and photonic architectures has complex edge weights instead, whose phases determine whether alternative routes interfere constructively or destructively. These architectures are also bipartite, so triangles are absent and the smallest closed cycle is a four-node square. Existing measures address complex weights and bipartite structure separately: bipartite clustering coefficients quantify clustering through four-node squares but do not contain phase information, while interferometric coefficients retain phase but are defined on triangles. In this work, we define a clustering coefficient for complex-weighted bipartite networks which reduces to the classical bipartite coefficient when the phases vanish, becomes negative when alternative routes cancel, and can be obtained for all nodes from a single sparse matrix product. papers.title: Femtosecond Three-Dimensional Imaging of Single-Protein with Hard X-ray Laser
papers.abs: The extreme intensity of X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses has enabled imaging of radiation-sensitive samples, such as macromolecular microcrystals, beyond radiation damage limits. These sources have the potential to enable biomolecular single-particle imaging, similar to cryo-electron microscopy but without the need for cryo-fixation and with temporal resolution from femtoseconds to milliseconds. While this possibility was recognized before XFELs were built, the biological single-particle imaging work flow has previously only been demonstrated on large virus particles. Building on improvements in X-ray beam focusing, particle delivery, diffraction detection, and advanced analysis, here we demonstrate imaging of a single molecular complex, the giant-hemoglobin erythrocruorin (Ery) with X-ray laser pulses. Two-dimensional classes of diffraction patterns could be reconstructed to 15 Angstrom resolution, and 3D images to ~20 to 30 Angstrom, even though the 3D merged intensity in reciprocal space extended beyond 20 Angstrom. papers.abs: Achieving and quantifying ultrastrong magnon-magnon coupling (USC) remains a key challenge for quantum magnonics. Here, we demonstrate widely tunable USC between chiral (right- and left-handed) and acoustic or optical magnon modes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet $CrPS_4$. Using a full quantum model, we decompose the interaction into three microscopic interaction channels: the co-rotating term $g_1$ (mode hybridization), the counter-rotating term $g_2$ (two-mode squeezing), and, uniquely in the chiral regime, the self-squared term $g_3$ that mediates single-mode squeezing. The normalized coupling ratio reaches $g/f_g$ $\sim$ 0.41, entering the USC regime. Most significantly, we establish a complete protocol linking these USC parameters to a measurable quantum phenomenon: a squeezed magnon vacuum state. Our simulations not only visualize the chirality and polarization evolution of the hybrid modes but also demonstrate how to directly extract quadrature fluctuations and a substantial squeezing factor (up to $\sim$ 9.7 dB) from thermal noise-driven magnetization dynamics. papers.abs: We report, to the best of our knowledge, the first controlled, like-for-like experimental mapping of how four practical design parameters--seed-cavity topology, seed power, amplifier pumping geometry, and seed-cavity free spectral range (FSR)--jointly shape the radio-frequency (RF)-resolved relative intensity noise (RIN) of high-power continuous-wave (CW) Yb-doped fiber lasers. We compare a standalone bidirectional fiber Bragg grating (FBG) oscillator, an FBG-seeded master-oscillator power amplifier (MOPA), and unidirectional ring-seeded MOPAs with FSRs of approximately 11.5 and 5 MHz, all near 1064 nm at a common 72 W output, with RIN measured from 10 kHz to 1 GHz. Across all settings, the low-frequency RIN is technical-noise limited and nearly architecture-independent, whereas RIN above 160 kHz is governed by the seed-cavity topology and its transfer through the amplifier. papers.abs: Van der Waals ferromagnets possess finite interlayer magnetic coupling despite their layered crystal structures, and this coupling plays an important role in determining their magnetic properties. Both temperatures exhibit pronounced pressure dependences, in sharp contrast to the nearly pressure-independent Curie temperature associated with intralayer ferromagnetic order. papers.abs: Extracting spectral properties such as energy position, broadening, and spectral weight from dielectric spectra is critical for interpreting collective electronic excitations in many-body physics. Conventional approaches typically rely on nonlinear fitting procedures that can be computationally demanding and highly sensitive to initialization and fitting choices. In this work, we develop a convolutional neural-network framework for the direct inversion of dielectric spectra into their underlying plasmonic pole structures using a multipole-Padé representation. Rather than training on a constrained database of spectra associated with a specific set of materials, the network is trained entirely on synthetic spectra generated from the analytical multipole-Padé expression with randomized parameters. This enables the network to learn the general mapping between the spectra and their features in an unbiased way, without requiring large, material-specific datasets derived from real materials. papers.abs: Quantum optical sensing has evolved from isolated solid state spin defect platforms to increasingly bio-integrated systems designed for biomedical applications. This review presents a perspective on this transition, spanning nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond to emerging fluorescent protein based spin qubits. Advances in diamond fabrication have enabled photonic cavities, nanomechanical resonators, and microstructured devices that enhance spin photon interactions and room temperature sensitivity. Exploration of spin defects in alternative materials further expands the sensing landscape. Parallel progress toward biological compatibility includes chip based architectures for in vitro and in vivo studies, microfluidic integration, and minimally invasive nanodiamond probes capable of intracellular nanothermometry and nanorheometry. Improvements in surface functionalization have enhanced coherence and sensing reliability in complex environments. Collectively, these advances highlight the progress and remaining challenges toward application oriented quantum sensing for the life sciences.

papers.abs: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) characterization is central to understanding quantum materials such as valley Hall and Rashba systems and, through its connection to Berry curvature, provides key insight into band topology. Here, we demonstrate a real-space approach to map the $L_z$ OAM character using scanning tunneling microscopy in triangular atomic monolayers. This shifts the local density of states (LDOS) maxima to distinct Wyckoff positions between atoms, encoding $L_z$ information into characteristic real-space LDOS patterns. papers.abs: We present a systematic study of the effects of chlorine substitution on the magneto-optical properties of the van der Waals layered semiconductor CrSBr. Our study shows that even at substitution level of $x=56\%$ the $\mathrm{CrSBr_{1-x}Cl_{x}}$ material exhibits qualitatively the same clear magneto-optical coupling that was observed in pure CrSBr crystals. The values of the relevant parameters are shown to vary smoothly across different substitution levels, thus offering promising tunability for this family of 2D magnetic materials.

papers.title: Learning qBIC Resonances across Metasurface Families in Dielectric Fourier Space
papers.abs: Bound states in the continuum (BIC) metasurfaces are typically described by geometry-specific parameters, hindering cross-geometry comparison, while ultranarrow qBIC features are easily diluted in full-spectrum learning. Here, 2015 samples from seven dielectric metasurface families are mapped to a shared reciprocal-lattice grid, where two frozen low-order Fourier channels capture resonance shifts with mean within-branch $R^2$ values of 0.871-0.999. Field-level analysis of two representative branches further confirms that these shifts are consistent with the Maxwell-Fourier perturbation picture. A five-channel K-space backbone models the broadband spectrum, while a local complex K-space expert parameterizes the qBIC resonance through a differentiable Fano layer. The expert reduces resonance-position mean absolute error (MAE) from 3.2 to 0.95 nm and the resonance-depth error by 14-fold on a geometry-blocked test set. The same coordinate supports spectrum-to-structure reconstruction.

papers.title: Topological Superradiant Universality Classes in Cavity-Mediated Spin Chains
papers.abs: Superradiant phase transitions are fundamental phenomena in light-matter coupled systems. Here, we uncover a novel class of superradiant criticality that is topologically distinct from previously known superradiant transitions. Using cavity-mediated cluster-Ising chains as an illustrative example, we numerically demonstrate that the critical line separating the superradiant phase from the cavity topological phase hosts robust symmetry-protected edge degeneracies, a feature absent in conventional superradiant transitions. Remarkably, although its local bulk critical properties are indistinguishable from those of the previously identified topologically trivial superradiant transition, the two criticalities cannot be smoothly connected without breaking the protecting symmetries or passing through a multicritical point. We further show that such topological superradiant criticality is generic, also occurring in cavity-mediated $\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{}$ cluster-qudit chains, as supported by complementary lattice simulations.

papers.title: Laser fragmentation in liquid - constructing a generic reaction map
papers.abs: Excitation of absorbing colloids in liquid by pulsed laser irradiation creates highly non-equilibrium states of matter that relax via defined pathways of thermal and non-thermal dissipation channels. The structural fingerprint of these channels can be probed by ultrafast {\it in situ} x-ray scattering methods and classified as a function of temporal delay of excitation excitation density, or specifically laser fluence. We study the example of photo-excitation of a gold colloid by picosecond laser pulses at the interband absorption band at 400 nm in water. By quantifying lattice temperature, crystalline fraction, particle sizes and the structural response of the water around the nanoparticles a reaction map is constructed that allows to pinpoint heating, particle melting, water bubble formation and finally particle fragmentation to form nanoclusters of predominant sizes of < 3 nm for applications in theranostics, photonics or catalysis.

papers.title: Simulations of Fluorescence and Energy Transfer in Periodic Systems: Pitfalls and Considerations for Bound States in the Continuum
papers.abs: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) combine high quality factors with strong electromagnetic-field localization and are therefore widely explored for enhancing light--matter interactions. However, large field amplitudes do not directly translate into useful fluorescence enhancement or energy transfer enhancement between two donor--acceptor fluorophores. Here, we investigate this question for a hybrid plasmonic--photonic resonant waveguide grating supporting a symmetry-protected BIC. We emphasize some of the pitfalls associated with the numerical simulations, especially the utilization of periodic boundary conditions for fluorescence. Strong BIC-related fields can enhance acceptor absorption while useful fluorescence enhancement remains moderate. Extensive simulations and the comparison of different figures of merit, indicate that, while a BIC can suppress radiative leakage, it can also redirect a large fraction of the energy into Ohmic losses.
